newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's de Silguy proposes 2001 introduction of euro notes.
newsitem.headline: EU's de Silguy proposes 2001 introduction of euro notes.

text.p: European Monetary Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy proposed on Thursday shortening the six-month period of dual circulation of the euro and national currencies, starting in the year 2002.
He also told a conference that public introduction of euro bank notes and coins should start in the autumn of 2001, ahead of the planned January 1, 2002 start date.

Under the planned scenario for the introduction of a single European currency, bank notes and coins would be put into public circulation three years after the 1999 launch date. But consumer groups have argued that introducing notes and coins on January 1, 2002 would be difficult given the traditional Christmas retail rush.
The suggested six-month period of dual circulation for the euro and national currencies has also been criticised for being too long.
